hits.hook: Today we are rolling out Gemini 4 Argon globally in the Gemini API, to Pro + Ultra in Gemini App, and Ultra subs in Antigravity!  Argon is a huge step forward for Gemini, and a lab
hits.text:
Today we are rolling out Gemini 4 Argon globally in the Gemini API, to Pro + Ultra in Gemini App, and Ultra subs in Antigravity!

Argon is a huge step forward for Gemini, and a labor of love. This model has been battle tested by over 100,000 people at Google over the last month, with so much new innovation, ambition, and hard work baked into this release. The team has been heads down over the last 6 months working to make this possible across the stack (research, infra, safety, eng, etc).

We rolled the model out to cyber defenders as part of our fairwind program and early access customers over the last 2 weeks, it has been amazing to see and talk to folks who are now using this model daily. Seeing the models writing capability, raw knowledge and persistence for coding, paired with new features like 1M token output when the model needs to work more has gotten me even more excited about our path ahead.

This is just the start of the Gemini 4 era. As you saw with 3.5, 3.6, 3.7, and 3.8 Flash, our iteration speed with Gemini is fast : ) Now with Gemini 4 Argon to work from, I am cannot wait to see the progress continue, and most importantly see what this new model enables for the world. 

This is such a special moment in the arc of technology, as millions of people everyday tackle problems they could never have thought possible before. Gemini 4 Argon was built to help you tackle the hardest problems. I have personally felt this spark with Argon and hope you do too. Onwards!!
hits.draft_en: Gemini 4 Argon rolling out globally in the API, another model drop and the accelerationists are eating good :D

THIS IS ACTUAL F*CKING GOLD

Anthropic employee leaked a Claude Code kit to stop it wasting expensive AI on easy jobs.

It's called jev-kit.

You know when Claude sends a powerful model to find a file or look something up?

This kit checks whether a cheaper agent could handle it.

Claude writes the code. JEV checks which jobs need the expensive help.

here's how it works:

> one tier too expensive? suggest a cheaper agent
> two or more tiers too expensive? block it in enforce mode and suggest the cheaper option
> agent says "done" without checking its work? send it back to verify
> tool call looks questionable? check it before it runs

The point is simple.

> Keep the powerful models for difficult work. Stop spending their time on basic searches and small decisions.

There's also an optional browser agent:

> JEV chooses what to click
> Claude writes the text that goes into fields
> a Sonnet planner can help when the steps aren't obvious

So instead of asking a big model to think through every click, you give it the parts that need actual writing and planning.

How much does it save?

There's no proven percentage for the whole kit. That depends on your tasks and which agents you're using.

But it gives you a way to spot expensive dispatches and test cheaper alternatives in your own workflow.

Start in shadow mode. It logs what it would flag without blocking anything.

Look at the results. Then decide what to enforce.

You'll need a TypeSafe API key for JEV.

paste this into Claude Code:

"Inspect https://t.co/K9iwgn5Qsa and read docs/install.md.

Run install/install.sh --check-only and show me the plan.

Explain how it could reduce expensive subagent use in my workflow and check whether it supports my current setup.

Show every settings change first. Keep shadow mode enabled.

Tell me where to enter my TYPESAFE_API_KEY locally, outside this chat.

No installation or changes until I approve."

https://t.co/1mnVQdzqlW

Your best model shouldn't spend its day looking for files.
